about: A rewrite of Linux system tools like mount and hexdump in Rust, aiming to match util-linux.

prs.title: hexdump now reports the right last offset when it skips past the end
prs.broken: When told to skip more bytes than the files hold, hexdump printed the amount you asked to skip as the last offset. The original tool prints the real size of the input, and nothing at all for an empty file.
prs.changed: Files that the skip covers whole are now counted by their real size. Input that can't be measured, like a pipe or a device, still reports the requested skip.
prs.matters: Scripts that read hexdump's offsets get the same numbers as with the original tool.

prs.title: mountpoint now checks the right folder and exits like util-linux
prs.broken: The mountpoint tool compared a path with the parent of the folder it was run from, not the path's own parent, so the answer depended on where you ran it. It also always exited with success.
prs.changed: On Linux it now asks the kernel's mount list, so bind mounts and mounts on files are found, and it falls back to the old check without /proc. Exit codes match util-linux.
prs.matters: Scripts that use mountpoint get the right answer and exit code.
